import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Create a figure and an axes object for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

# Create a bar plot to visualize survival rate by passenger class and sex
# 'survived' is a binary variable (0 or 1), so the mean directly represents the survival rate.
sns.barplot(data=df, x='pclass', y='survived', hue='sex', palette='viridis', errorbar='ci')

# Add titles and labels for clarity
plt.title('Survival Rate on Titanic by Passenger Class and Sex', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Passenger Class', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Survival Rate', fontsize=12)

# Customize x-axis tick labels for better readability
# Mapping pclass numbers to descriptive names
pclass_labels = {1: 'First Class', 2: 'Second Class', 3: 'Third Class'}
plt.xticks(ticks=[0, 1, 2], labels=[pclass_labels[1], pclass_labels[2], pclass_labels[3]], fontsize=10)

# Ensure y-axis starts at 0 and goes up to 1 for survival rate
plt.ylim(0, 1)

# Add a legend
plt.legend(title='Sex', loc='upper right')

# Add a grid for easier reading of values
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Save the figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
